rules.title: No heavy library for a minor need
rules.what: Do not add a library for what the platform or a few lines of code already do; import only the functions actually used.
rules.why: The classic case: a full utility library (or a UI framework) imported for two helpers. The whole package is parsed, bundled and shipped to every user for those two calls.
rules.how: Check for a native API first; if the library is justified, import the specific module (e.g. lodash/get -> a 3-line function) and let tree-shaking prove it.

patterns.note: Default import of a known-heavy library; count actual usage.
moment is legacy-heavy; date-fns/dayjs or Intl cover most needs.

verify.how: Bundle analysis shows the library's measured weight and the use count justifying it.

limits: A library heavily used is legitimate; the rule targets one-function and duplicate-platform imports.

rules.title: Load on demand
rules.what: Load code and assets when they are needed (route-level code splitting, dynamic import, lazy loading below the fold), not upfront.
rules.why: Bytes the user never reaches are pure cost. Code splitting moves that cost from every visit to the visits that actually see the feature.
rules.how: Split per route or per heavy component; lazy-load below-the-fold media and embeds (native loading=lazy, IntersectionObserver facades); preload only what the next step needs.

verify.how: Bundle map shows per-route chunks; initial bundle contains only the critical journey.

limits: Splitting adds request overhead; group chunks sensibly instead of one file per component.

rules.title: No blocking or synchronous requests
rules.what: No synchronous XHR, no blocking scripts in head without defer/async, no render-blocking third-party CSS.
rules.why: A blocking request holds the whole page hostage to the slowest item: the user's device burns battery and data on a blank screen.
rules.how: Use fetch with async patterns; add defer/async to scripts; inline critical CSS, load the rest with media tricks; measure the waterfall.

patterns.note: Sync XHR candidate; verify it is not async-wrapped.
External script without defer/async; blocking by default.

verify.how: No sync XHR; scripts carry defer/async or are at end of body; waterfall shows no long blocking chain.

rules.title: DOM neither too large nor too deep
rules.what: Keep the DOM small and shallow: no lists of thousands of rendered nodes, no deep wrapper nesting, virtualise long lists.
rules.why: DOM size drives memory, style recalculation and reflow on every change; deep nesting multiplies the cost of each update on low-end devices.
rules.how: Paginate or virtualise long lists, remove wrapper divs that exist for one CSS rule, prefer semantic elements over div stacks.

patterns.note: Four-level div nesting; candidate for structural review.

verify.how: Node count on the main views within budget (e.g. < 1500 nodes); measured on the minimum device profile.

limits: Virtualisation adds complexity; apply it to genuinely long lists, not to tens of items.

rules.title: No dead code and no dead CSS
rules.what: Remove code and styles that nothing references: unused exports, orphan CSS rules, legacy hacks for browsers no longer supported.
rules.why: Dead code is parsed, bundled and shipped on every load forever, for a runtime path that can no longer execute.
rules.how: Run an unused-export/coverage check and a purge on CSS at build; delete legacy browser hacks with the browser support policy.

patterns.note: Legacy browser hack patterns; obsolete with modern support policy.

verify.how: Coverage tool output shows unused-code ratio trending down; no hacks for unsupported browsers.

limits: Dynamic references (string-built class names) fool purge tools; review before deleting.

rules.title: CSS without duplication or !important escalation
rules.what: Keep CSS deduplicated: no repeated selectors/declarations across files, no !important escalation wars, no duplicate HTML ids.
rules.why: Duplicated CSS inflates the stylesheet the user parses on every page, and !important escalation is a maintenance debt that forces heavier and heavier overrides.
rules.how: Lint for duplicate rules; resolve specificity properly instead of escalating; the build fails on duplicate ids.

patterns.note: Count occurrences; a few are legitimate (overrides of third-party styles), many indicate escalation.

verify.how: Duplication report clean or exceptions documented; no duplicate ids.

rules.title: Clean up listeners, timers and observers
rules.what: Every event listener, interval, timeout and observer added for a component's lifetime is removed when that lifetime ends.
rules.why: Leaked listeners keep objects, closures and callbacks alive across route changes; on a long session they turn into real memory growth and background CPU.
rules.how: Register cleanup in the component's teardown path (unmount hook, abort controller, removeEventListener); abort fetches on unmount.

patterns.note: Interval created; verify a matching clearInterval in teardown.
Listener added; verify symmetric removal if scoped to a component.

verify.how: Memory snapshot flat across repeated mount/unmount cycles; no pending timers after teardown.

limits: Document-level listeners that outlive components are deliberate; document them.

rules.title: Debounce and throttle user-driven compute
rules.what: Compute driven by user input (search-as-you-type, resize, scroll, mousemove) is debounced or throttled; heavy recomputation does not run per keystroke or per pixel.
rules.why: Per-event processing multiplies work by the user's activity rate, which can be hundreds of events a second; the results are usually discarded before being seen.
rules.how: Debounce input-driven requests (300 ms is a common value, measure yours), throttle visual updates, and cancel superseded work (abort in-flight requests).

patterns.note: High-frequency event listener; verify debounce/throttle in the handler.

verify.how: Request/compute count per interaction task within budget; no superseded work completing.

limits: Immediate feedback (cursor, text) must not be debounced; target the expensive part only.

rules.title: Defer what is deferrable, keep what the user waits for
rules.what: Defer the loading of non-critical scripts and features; never defer what the user's first action on the page needs.
rules.why: Deferring everything just moves the cost to the moment of use; deferring nothing taxes every visit. The split must follow the critical journey, not a rule of thumb.
rules.how: Identify the above-the-fold interaction; everything it needs is eager, the rest is deferred/lazy. Measure LCP/TTI on the minimum profile after the split.

verify.how: LCP and interaction latency on the minimum device profile meet the stated budget.

rules.title: Minify and compress transport
rules.what: Serve text assets minified, over HTTP compression (gzip/brotli), with correct media types; images compressed at build (see NR-CONTENT-001).
rules.why: Minification and transport compression are the cheapest bytes ever saved: no code change, no risk, pure configuration on the delivery path.
rules.how: Minify at build (JS/CSS/HTML/SVG), enable brotli/gzip at the server or CDN, verify Content-Encoding in production.

verify.how: Production responses carry Content-Encoding: br/gzip; asset sizes match minified output.

rules.title: No avoidable requests
rules.what: Remove non-essential and duplicate requests from the main user journeys and keep a request budget per page.
rules.why: Every request costs a round trip, server work and radio time; duplicates and trackers add cost without serving the user.
rules.how: Audit the journey's network trace; deduplicate fetches; drop unused third parties; set a request and weight budget in CI.

verify.how: Production network trace of the main journeys checked against the request budget.
